title: Speaking openly and seeing differently
meaning: Your conversation can stay open and gentle even when what you hear requires a pause and a different perspective.
text: Openness in your shared voice can look simple: naming what is happening so neither person has to guess. The Sun in the physical position of Vishuddha gives speech this clear, warm quality. Strength in energy sustains the courage to remain kind when the subject is difficult. The Hanged Man in emotions describes a particular response to what you hear: needing to pause, set aside a ready answer and see the question from an unfamiliar angle. That pause can belong to real understanding and participation.

Imagine hearing after a meal together, “I found it hard to keep up with that conversation.” You can let the words settle before explaining why everything seemed to go well. **Honesty brings you closer when an answer has time to form.** A warm tone leaves room for something beyond instantly cheering each other up. Sometimes you can simply stay beside a new thought. Later, it becomes clearer which part of the evening felt difficult and what had previously been hard to say.

It gets harder if openness becomes a stream of words while the other's inner pause seems like an obstacle. Wanting an answer quickly to restore ease can lead to more questions. The person listening has less room to find a sentence of their own. Warmth remains available when silence also has an understandable place between you.
